example.fact: 拟 often appears in 拟定 (nǐdìng, "to draw up, draft") and 模拟 (mónǐ, "to simulate"), common in formal and technical writing.

meanings: to present a memorial to the emperor (old)

example.fact: 奏 today most often appears in 演奏 (yǎnzòu, "to perform music"), a shift from its older meaning of presenting reports to the emperor.

etymologyHint: To walk 辶 by the river 巛; 巛 also provides the pronunciation

example.fact: 巡 almost always appears together with 逻 in 巡逻 (xúnluó, "to patrol"), rarely standing alone in modern speech.

components.note: 页 (from 頁, head) relates 颜 to the face, part of the head.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu de yánsè hěn piàoliang.

example.fact: 颜 combines with 色 to form 颜色 (yánsè, "color"), its most common use today, though 颜 alone once meant "face" or "countenance."

meanings: classifier for a dose of medicine

components.note: 刂 (knife) relates 剂 to cutting or dividing something into a prepared dose.

example.fact: 绩 almost always appears in 成绩 (chéngjì, "grades, results"), a word every student in China hears often.

example.fact: 贡 usually appears in 贡献 (gòngxiàn, "contribution"), extending its old meaning of "tribute offered to the emperor."

components.note: 疒 (sickness) shows 疯 describes an afflicted state of mind.

components.note: 土 (earth) shows 坡 relates to a feature of the ground.
皮 (pí) gives a sound close to pō, sharing the initial consonant though the vowel differs.

components.note: 目 (eye) shows 瞧 relates to looking or seeing.
焦 (jiāo) gives a sound distantly related to qiáo, having drifted apart in the initial consonant over time.

example.english: Look, what's that?
example.fact: 瞧 is a colloquial synonym for 看 (kàn, "to look"), often used to draw someone's attention, as in 你瞧 (nǐ qiáo, "look here").

etymologyHint: A bird 隹 cut off from its nest 十 by a weapon 戈

components.note: 火 (fire) shows 燃 relates directly to burning.

etymologyHint: A bird 隹 getting its tail singed 灬

example.pinyin: Gùgōng yǒu hěn duō dà diàn.

components.note: 亻 (person) shows 伪 describes something false or counterfeit, often about people's actions or claims.

components.note: 木 (tree) shows 柳 names a type of tree.

components.note: 钅 (metal) shows 锁 is typically a metal object.
⺌ (a form of 小) gives a sound distantly related to suǒ, having drifted apart over time.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) shows 逼 relates to movement, as in pressing someone toward an action.

etymologyHint: Th sun 日 setting behind a village 氏

圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to jiā, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí ràng tā hěn kùnhuò.
example.english: This problem left him very confused.
example.fact: 惑 usually appears in 困惑 (kùnhuò, "confused, puzzled") and 疑惑 (yíhuò, "doubt, confusion").

etymologyHint: A mound 阝 of clay 匋; 匋 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 阝 (mound, earth) on the left relates to earthen material.
匋 (a clay vessel) on the right shows the object being shaped, giving 陶 its meaning 'pottery, ceramics.'

example.english: She likes making pottery.
example.fact: 陶 appears in 陶瓷 (táocí, "ceramics, porcelain") and 陶器 (táoqì, "pottery"), core vocabulary for describing clay crafts.

etymologyHint: An animal with horns 丷, eyes 田, nose 一, and mouth 口

components.note: 丷 (horns) at the top shows the animal's horns.
田 (here shaped like a head with eyes) in the middle represents the animal's face.
口 (mouth) at the bottom completes the creature's face, giving 兽 its meaning 'beast, animal.'

example.english: The tiger is a kind of wild beast.
example.fact: 兽 appears in 野兽 (yěshòu, "wild beast") and 怪兽 (guàishòu, "monster"), usually describing large or fierce animals rather than pets.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) shows 帐 relates to something made of fabric, like a tent or curtain.
长 (zhǎng) gives a sound close to zhàng, sharing the initial consonant.

example.hanzi: 他们在山里搭了一个帐篷。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài shān lǐ dā le yí gè zhàngpéng.
example.english: They set up a tent in the mountains.
example.fact: 帐 appears in 帐篷 (zhàngpéng, "tent") and 帐户 (zhànghù, "bank account"), covering both camping gear and finance.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) reflects 饰's original connection to adornment made of cloth or fabric.
饣 (a form of 食, shí) gives a sound close to shì, sharing the initial consonant.

example.english: She likes wearing jewelry.
example.fact: 饰 appears in 首饰 (shǒushì, "jewelry") and 装饰 (zhuāngshì, "to decorate"), both about adornment.

components.note: 贝 (money) shows 贷 relates to a financial transaction.
代 (dài) gives the exact sound of 贷.

example.pinyin: Tā xiàng yínháng dàikuǎn mǎi fáng.
example.english: He took out a loan from the bank to buy a house.
example.fact: 贷 usually appears in 贷款 (dàikuǎn, "loan") and 信用贷 (xìnyòngdài, "credit loan"), core banking vocabulary.

etymologyHint: Speaking 曰 in the daytime 日

components.note: 日 (sun, day) on top represents daytime.
曰 (to speak) below shows words being spoken, giving 昌 its meaning 'flourishing, prosperous' – an auspicious image of open, bright speech.

example.pinyin: Chāng shì yí gè chángjiàn de míngzi.
example.english: Chang is a common name.
example.fact: 昌 means "flourishing, prosperous" and is a popular character in Chinese given names and place names, like 南昌 (Nánchāng), a city in Jiangxi.

meanings: abbr. for Syria 敘利亞|叙利亚[Xu4 li4 ya4]

components.note: 又 (hand) shows 叙 relates to an action, here recounting or relating something.
余 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to xù, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他给我叙述了整个故事。
example.pinyin: Tā gěi wǒ xùshù le zhěnggè gùshi.
example.english: He narrated the whole story to me.
example.fact: 叙 appears in 叙述 (xùshù, "to narrate") and 叙旧 (xùjiù, "to reminisce about old times"), both about recounting things.

components.note: 身 (body) shows 躺 relates to an action of the body.
尚 (shàng) gives a sound distantly related to tǎng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā tǎng zài chuáng shang xiūxi.
example.english: He lies on the bed resting.
example.fact: 躺 is the standard verb for lying down, as in 躺下 (tǎngxià, "to lie down"), distinct from 坐 (zuò, "to sit") and 站 (zhàn, "to stand").

components.note: 钅 (metal) shows 钢 names a type of metal.
冈 (gāng) gives the exact sound of 钢.

example.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo shì yòng gāng zuò de.
example.english: This bridge is made of steel.
example.fact: 钢 appears in 钢铁 (gāngtiě, "steel") and 钢琴 (gāngqín, "piano," literally "steel-string instrument"), both common compound words.

components.note: 氵 (water) shows 沟 relates to a channel for water.
勾 (gōu) gives the exact sound of 沟.

example.hanzi: 雨后路边的沟里有很多水。
example.pinyin: Yǔ hòu lùbiān de gōu lǐ yǒu hěn duō shuǐ.
example.english: After the rain there's a lot of water in the roadside ditch.
example.fact: 沟 names a ditch or gully, and appears figuratively in 沟通 (gōutōng, "to communicate," literally "to connect a channel").

meanings: to entrust; to place in sb's care
to send by post; to mail

components.note: 宀 (roof) shows 寄 relates to a household, as in sending something from home.
奇 (qí) gives a sound distantly related to jì, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Wǒ gěi māma jì le yì fēng xìn.
example.english: I mailed a letter to my mom.
example.fact: 寄 is the standard verb for mailing or sending something by post, as in 寄信 (jì xìn, "to mail a letter").

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows 扶 relates to physically supporting something with the hand.
夫 (fū) gives a sound close to fú, differing mainly in tone.

example.english: He supports grandma while walking.
example.fact: 扶 means to support someone physically, as in 扶老人 (fú lǎorén, "help an elderly person") and 扶手 (fúshǒu, "handrail").

components.note: 钅 (metal) reflects the character's old sense tied to metal goods laid out for display in a shop, the source of 铺's meaning "shop."
甫 (fǔ) gives a sound distantly related to pù, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Jiējiǎo yǒu yì jiā xiǎo pùzi.
example.english: There's a small shop on the street corner.
example.fact: 铺 (pù) means "shop, store," as in 店铺 (diànpù, "shop"); the same character read pū means "to spread out," a common case of one character with two readings.

components.note: 阝 (mound, place) shows 邓 is originally a place name, later a surname.
登 (dēng) gives a sound close to dèng, differing mainly in tone.

example.english: Deng is a surname.
example.fact: 邓 is best known as the surname of Deng Xiaoping (邓小平), a key leader in modern Chinese history.

components.note: 寿 evolved as an altered, simplified form of 老 (old), extending its meaning to 'long life, longevity.'

example.english: We wish grandpa a long life.
example.fact: 寿 means "longevity," and appears in 长寿 (chángshòu, "long life") and 寿星 (shòuxīng, "the birthday person," especially an elder).

components.note: 忄 (heart) shows 惧 relates to an emotion.
具 (jù) gives the exact sound of 惧.

example.english: He is afraid of the dark.
example.fact: 惧 usually appears in 恐惧 (kǒngjù, "fear, dread") and 惧怕 (jùpà, "to be afraid of"), more formal than 怕 (pà) alone.

components.note: 讠 (speech) shows 询 relates to asking or speaking.
旬 (xún) gives the exact sound of 询.

example.english: I'd like to inquire about the price.
example.fact: 询 appears in 询问 (xúnwèn, "to inquire") and 咨询 (zīxún, "to consult"), common in customer service and formal requests.

components.note: 氵 (water) shows 汤 relates to a liquid, as in soup or broth.
昜 (yáng) gives a sound distantly related to tāng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Māma zuò le yì wǎn tāng.
example.english: Mom made a bowl of soup.
example.fact: 汤 is the everyday word for soup or broth, as in 鸡汤 (jītāng, "chicken soup"), and is also a common surname.

example.english: The bank was robbed.
example.fact: 盗 appears in 盗窃 (dàoqiè, "to steal") and 强盗 (qiángdào, "robber, bandit"), both about theft.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) shows 肥 relates to a bodily state.
巴 (bā) gives a sound distantly related to féi, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhī māo tài féi le.
example.english: This cat is too fat.
example.fact: 肥 describes fatness, as in 肥胖 (féipàng, "obese"), and also means "fertile," as in 肥料 (féiliào, "fertilizer").

components.note: 云 here stands in for an older form meaning "to speak of, to taste," 尝's core meaning.
尚 (shàng) gives a sound distantly related to cháng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ cháng yíxià zhège cài.
example.english: You can try tasting this dish.
example.fact: 尝 is the verb for tasting food, as in 尝一尝 (cháng yi cháng, "give it a taste"), and also means "to experience," as in 尝试 (chángshì, "to attempt").

example.english: He left in a great hurry.
example.fact: 匆 almost always appears doubled or with 忙, as in 匆忙 (cōngmáng, "hastily") and 匆匆 (cōngcōng, "hurriedly").

components.note: 光 (light) shows 辉 relates to brightness or radiance.
军 (jūn) gives a sound distantly related to huī, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: His achievements are brilliant and glorious.
example.fact: 辉 almost always appears in 辉煌 (huīhuáng, "brilliant, glorious") and 光辉 (guānghuī, "radiance"), describing dazzling light or great achievement.

etymologyHint: A man 大 with spirit 示

components.note: 大 (a person, from the pictograph of a standing figure) forms the main part of the character.
示 (spirit, altar) suggests a person before the spirits, expressing helplessness, giving 奈 its meaning 'how, what can be done' as in 无奈 (helpless).

example.pinyin: Tā hěn wúnài, zhǐ néng děngdài.
example.english: He was helpless and could only wait.
example.fact: 奈 almost always appears in 无奈 (wúnài, "helpless, having no choice") and 奈何 (nàihé, "what can be done about it").

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows 扣 relates to an action done by hand, like fastening a button.
口 (kǒu) gives a sound close to kòu, sharing the initial consonant.

example.pinyin: Tā kòu hǎo le yīfu de kòuzi.
example.english: He buttoned up his clothes.
example.fact: 扣 names a button (扣子, kòuzi) and the action of fastening or deducting, as in 打折扣 (dǎ zhékòu, "to give a discount").

components.note: 廴 (a form related to slow walking) relates 廷 to a place one moves through, as in a palace courtyard.

example.english: In ancient times there was an imperial court.
example.fact: 廷 rarely stands alone in modern Chinese – it almost always appears in 朝廷 (cháotíng, "the imperial court"), a historical term.

meanings: Macao (abbr. for 澳門|澳门[Ao4 men2])
Australia (abbr. for 澳大利亞|澳大利亚[Ao4 da4 li4 ya4])

components.note: 氵 (water) shows 澳 relates to a body of water, like a bay or inlet.
奥 (ào) gives the exact sound of 澳.

example.english: He traveled to Australia.
example.fact: 澳 mostly appears in 澳洲 or 澳大利亚 (Àozhōu, Àodàlìyà, "Australia") and 澳门 (Àomén, "Macau"), both place names.

meanings: used in 唵嘛呢叭咪吽[an3 ma2 ni2 ba1 mi1 hong1]
modal particle indicating that sth is obvious
particle indicating a pause for emphasis

components.note: 口 (mouth) shows 嘛 relates to speech, as a spoken particle.
麻 (má) gives a sound close to ma, differing mainly in tone.

example.english: Just go!
example.fact: 嘛 is a spoken particle that softens a suggestion or marks something as obvious, common in casual conversation rather than a word with its own meaning.

components.note: 艹 (plant) reflects 董's original meaning related to a type of plant, later used for "to direct, supervise" and as a surname.
重 (zhòng) gives a sound distantly related to dǒng, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: He is the company's chairman.
example.fact: 董 appears in 董事 (dǒngshì, "director, board member") and 董事长 (dǒngshìzhǎng, "chairman of the board"), common in business vocabulary.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) shows 迁 relates to movement from one place to another.
千 (qiān) gives the exact sound of 迁.

example.hanzi: 他们全家搬迁到了北京。
example.pinyin: Tāmen quánjiā bānqiān dào le Běijīng.
example.english: Their whole family relocated to Beijing.
example.fact: 迁 usually appears in 搬迁 (bānqiān, "to relocate") and 迁移 (qiānyí, "to migrate"), about moving from one place to another.

components.note: 冫 (ice) shows 凝 relates to something solidifying, like liquid turning to ice.
疑 (yí) gives a sound distantly related to níng, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: Water froze into ice.
example.fact: 凝 usually appears in 凝结 (níngjié, "to condense, congeal") and 凝视 (níngshì, "to gaze intently"), covering both physical change and focused looking.

components.note: 心 (heart) shows 慰 relates to an emotional state.
尉 (wèi) gives the exact sound of 慰.

example.english: Her friend comforted her.
example.fact: 慰 almost always appears in 安慰 (ānwèi, "to comfort") and 慰问 (wèiwèn, "to express sympathy or concern").

meanings: (bound form) to loathe; to be fed up with

components.note: 厂 (a cliff shape) reflects 厌's original meaning related to a rock formation, later shifted to mean "to dislike."
犬 (quǎn) gives a sound distantly related to yàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: He really dislikes rainy days.
example.fact: 厌 usually appears in 讨厌 (tǎoyàn, "to dislike, annoying") and 厌烦 (yànfán, "to be fed up with").

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) shows 脏 (zàng) relates to the body, as in internal organs.
庄 (zhuāng) gives a sound close to zàng, sharing a similar consonant sound though the vowel and ending differ.

example.english: The heart beats every day.
example.fact: 脏 (zàng) names internal organs, as in 心脏 (xīnzàng, "heart") and 内脏 (nèizàng, "internal organs") – a different word from 脏 (zāng, "dirty"), read with a different tone.

components.note: 马 (horse) shows 腾 relates to swift movement, like a galloping horse.
朕 (zhèn) gives a sound distantly related to téng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ téngchū yìdiǎn shíjiān.
example.english: Please help me free up some time.
example.fact: 腾 appears in 腾出 (téngchū, "to free up, make available") and 奔腾 (bēnténg, "to gallop, surge"), both about swift movement or making space.

etymologyHint: Small niches 幺 in the mountainside 山; 幺 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 山 (mountain) surrounds the character, setting the scene.
幺 (small, doubled here) shows tiny hidden niches within the mountainside, giving 幽 its meaning 'secluded, hidden, dark.'

example.english: This valley is very secluded and quiet.
example.fact: 幽 usually appears in 幽静 (yōujìng, "tranquil, secluded") and 幽默 (yōumò, "humor," a phonetic loanword unrelated to its literal meaning).

components.note: 心 (heart) shows 怨 relates to an emotion.
夗 (yuàn) gives the exact sound of 怨.

example.english: He has no complaints.
example.fact: 怨 usually appears in 抱怨 (bàoyuàn, "to complain") and 怨恨 (yuànhèn, "resentment"), about lingering grievance.

components.note: 革 (leather) shows 鞋 is typically made of leather.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to xié, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā mǎi le yì shuāng xīn xié.
example.english: She bought a new pair of shoes.
example.fact: 鞋 is the everyday word for shoes, measured with 双 (shuāng, "pair"), as in 一双鞋 (yì shuāng xié).

etymologyHint: A lost 厶 jade 玉

components.note: 玉 (jade, shown without its dot) represents something valuable.
厶 beneath suggests something slipping away privately, giving 丢 its meaning 'to lose, to throw away.'

example.english: I lost my keys.
example.fact: 丢 is the common verb for losing or discarding something, as in 丢了 (diū le, "lost it") and 丢垃圾 (diū lājī, "throw away trash").

components.note: 土 (earth) shows 埋 relates to putting something into the ground.
里 (lǐ) gives a sound distantly related to mái, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Gǒu bǎ gǔtou mái zài tǔ lǐ le.
example.english: The dog buried the bone in the dirt.
example.fact: 埋 means "to bury," as in 埋葬 (máizàng, "to bury") – note it's also read mán in 埋怨 (mányuàn, "to complain"), a different tone for a different meaning.

etymologyHint: Water 水 flowing from a spring 白

components.note: 白 (here representing the spring's opening) sits above.
水 (water) below shows water flowing out, giving 泉 its meaning 'spring, fountain.'

example.english: There's a clear spring here.
example.fact: 泉 names a natural spring, as in 温泉 (wēnquán, "hot spring") – a popular travel destination in China.

meanings: to well up; to gush forth; to surge

components.note: 氵 (water) shows 涌 relates to the movement of a liquid, or by extension, a crowd.
甬 (yǒng) gives the exact sound of 涌.

example.english: The crowd surged toward the exit.
example.fact: 涌 describes a surging movement, as in 涌入 (yǒngrù, "to pour in") and 涌现 (yǒngxiàn, "to emerge in large numbers").

meanings: linchpin (used to fasten a wheel to an axle)
(bound form) to govern; to have jurisdiction over

components.note: 车 (cart) shows 辖 relates to a mechanical part of a cart or vehicle, extended to "to govern."
害 (hài) gives a sound distantly related to xiá, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: This area is under Beijing's jurisdiction.
example.fact: 辖 almost always appears in 管辖 (guǎnxiá, "to have jurisdiction over") and 辖区 (xiáqū, "jurisdiction area"), common in administrative and legal contexts.

components.note: 身 (body) shows 躲 relates to an action of the body, like hiding.
朵 (duǒ) gives the exact sound of 躲.

example.english: He hid behind the door.
example.fact: 躲 is the standard verb for hiding or dodging, as in 躲雨 (duǒ yǔ, "take shelter from the rain") and 躲避 (duǒbì, "to avoid, evade").

meanings: short name for Shanxi 山西[Shan1 xi1]
etymologyHint: An advance to the second 亚 day 日

components.note: 亚 (here a stylized shape related to advancing in rank) sits above.
日 (sun, day) below anchors the meaning in time, giving 晋 its sense 'to advance, to promote.'

example.pinyin: Tā shēngzhí le, jìnshēng wéi jīnglǐ.
example.english: He got promoted, advancing to manager.
example.fact: 晋 usually appears in 晋升 (jìnshēng, "to promote, be promoted") and is also the name of the ancient state and later dynasty of Jin (晋).

components.note: 糸 (silk thread) shows 紫 relates to dyed fabric, hence a color.
此 (cǐ) gives a sound close to zǐ, sharing a similar consonant sound.

example.english: The sky turned purple.
example.fact: 紫 names the color purple, as in 紫色 (zǐsè) and 紫外线 (zǐwàixiàn, "ultraviolet rays," literally "beyond-purple rays").

components.note: 艮 (stubborn, hard) shows 艰 relates to something difficult.
堇 (jǐn) gives a sound close to jiān, sharing the initial consonant.

example.english: Learning Chinese is very difficult.
example.fact: 艰 usually appears in 艰难 (jiānnán, "difficult, arduous") and 艰苦 (jiānkǔ, "hard, tough"), describing difficult conditions or effort.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) shows 魏 once related to a spirit or ghost sense, now mainly a surname and dynasty name.
委 (wěi) gives a sound close to wèi, differing mainly in tone.

example.hanzi: 魏是中国古代的一个国家。
example.pinyin: Wèi shì Zhōngguó gǔdài de yí gè guójiā.
example.english: Wei was an ancient state in China.
example.fact: 魏 names one of the Three Kingdoms (三国) of ancient China, and is also a common Chinese surname.

components.note: 口 (mouth) shows 吾 relates to speech, as a word for "I" used in speaking of oneself.
五 (wǔ) gives a sound close to wú, differing mainly in tone.

example.pinyin: Wú shì gǔdài rén shuō de "wǒ".
example.english: Wú is how ancient people said "I."
example.fact: 吾 is a classical Chinese word meaning "I, my," largely replaced by 我 (wǒ) in modern speech but still seen in old texts and set phrases.

meanings: to get panicky; to lose one's head

components.note: 忄 (heart) shows 慌 relates to an emotional state.
荒 (huāng) gives the exact sound of 慌.

example.english: Hearing the news, he became flustered.
example.fact: 慌 usually appears in 慌张 (huāngzhāng, "flustered, panicky") and 惊慌 (jīnghuāng, "alarmed, panic-stricken").

meanings: to wish (sb bon voyage, happy birthday etc)
etymologyHint: A person 兄 praying before an altar 礻

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit) on the left sets a religious scene.
兄 (a person, shown here kneeling or speaking) on the right shows someone praying, giving 祝 its meaning 'to wish, to pray for blessings.'

example.english: Happy birthday!
example.fact: 祝 is the go-to verb for well-wishes in Chinese, as in 祝你好运 (zhù nǐ hǎoyùn, "wish you good luck") and 祝贺 (zhùhè, "to congratulate").

components.note: 阝 (mound, place) shows 邮 relates to stations along a route, the origin of its postal meaning.
由 (yóu) gives the exact sound of 邮.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zài yóujú jì le bāoguǒ.
example.english: I mailed a package at the post office.
example.fact: 邮 relates to mail and post, as in 邮局 (yóujú, "post office") and 邮件 (yóujiàn, "mail, email").

components.note: 口 (mouth) shows 吐 relates to an action of the mouth.
土 (tǔ) gives the exact sound of 吐.

example.english: Please don't spit on the ground.
example.fact: 吐 (tǔ) means "to spit out," as in 吐痰 (tǔ tán, "to spit"); read tù (fourth tone) instead, the same character means "to vomit."

components.note: 犭 (dog) reflects an old association with fierce animals, extended to describe cruelty in 狠.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound distantly related to hěn, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: He is very harsh with the child.
example.fact: 狠 describes cruelty or severity, as in 心狠 (xīnhěn, "cruel-hearted") and 狠心 (hěnxīn, "hard-hearted, ruthless") – it's a homophone of, but different word from, 很 (hěn, "very").

components.note: 金 (metal) reflects 鉴's original meaning "a bronze mirror," an object made of metal.

example.hanzi: 我们可以借鉴他的经验。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen kěyǐ jièjiàn tā de jīngyàn.
example.english: We can learn from his experience.
example.fact: 鉴 usually appears in 借鉴 (jièjiàn, "to learn from, use as reference") and 鉴定 (jiàndìng, "to appraise, authenticate"), extending from "mirror" to "to examine, reflect on."

etymologyHint: Picture of an open 一 mouth 口

components.note: 曰 pictures an open mouth 口 with a stroke across it, representing words coming out, giving 曰 its meaning 'to say.'

example.hanzi: 古人说"曰"，就是"说"的意思。
example.english: Ancient people said "yuē," which means "to say."
example.fact: 曰 is a classical Chinese word for "to say," most familiar today from the phrase 子曰 (zǐ yuē, "Confucius says"), which opens many sayings in the Analects.

components.note: 木 (wood) shows 械 relates to a wooden tool or device, extended to "equipment."
戒 (jiè) gives a sound close to xiè, differing mainly in tone.

example.hanzi: 医院里有很多医疗器械。

example.fact: 冠 (guān) means "crown, cap," as in 皇冠 (huángguān, "crown"); read guàn (fourth tone) instead, the same character means "to rank first," as in 冠军 (guànjūn, "champion").

components.note: 米 (rice) shows 粒 relates to small grains.
立 (lì) gives the exact sound of 粒.

example.english: There's a grain of rice on the ground.
example.fact: 粒 is the measure word for small round things, as in 一粒米 (yí lì mǐ, "a grain of rice") and 一粒药 (yí lì yào, "a pill").

components.note: 辶 (to walk) shows 遥 relates to distance traveled.
䍃 gives a sound close to yáo, sharing the vowel sound.

example.pinyin: Nà zuò shān lí zhèlǐ hěn yáoyuǎn.
example.english: That mountain is very far from here.
example.fact: 遥 almost always appears in 遥远 (yáoyuǎn, "far away, remote") and 遥控 (yáokòng, "remote control").

components.note: 口 (mouth), shown here doubled, suggests two voices in harmony – 吕 was originally a term for a musical pitch, and later became a common surname.

example.pinyin: Lǚ shì yí gè chángjiàn de xìng.
example.english: Lü is a common surname.
example.fact: 吕 is a common Chinese surname and was historically also the name of one of the twelve pitches in ancient Chinese music theory.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì tīng qǐlai hěn xuán.
example.english: This matter sounds very mysterious.
example.fact: 玄 means "mysterious, profound," as in 玄妙 (xuánmiào, "mysterious, subtle") – a word often used to describe things hard to explain.

etymologyHint: Small 小 flakes of earth 土

components.note: 小 (small) on top shows tiny particles.
土 (earth) below is the material, giving 尘 its meaning 'dust, dirt.'

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu hěn duō huīchén.
example.english: There's a lot of dust on the table.
example.fact: 尘 usually appears in 灰尘 (huīchén, "dust") and 尘土 (chéntǔ, "dust, dirt"), and figuratively in 红尘 (hóngchén, "the mortal, earthly world" in literary contexts).

components.note: 马 (horse) reflects an old sense of 冯 related to galloping on horseback.
冫 (ice) gives a sound distantly related to féng, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: Feng is a surname.
example.fact: 冯 is mainly known today as a Chinese surname; the character also carries the classical senses "to gallop" and "by means of," though these are rarely used alone today.

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows 抚 relates to a gentle action done by hand.
无 (wú) gives a sound distantly related to fǔ, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Māma fǔmō zhe háizi de tóu.
example.english: Mom gently strokes the child's head.
example.fact: 抚 usually appears in 抚摸 (fǔmō, "to stroke, caress") and 安抚 (ānfǔ, "to soothe, pacify"), both about comforting or gentle touch.
